newsitem.title: USA: Texaco works to avoid Eugene Island delays.
newsitem.headline: Texaco works to avoid Eugene Island delays.

text.p: Texaco said on Tuesday that it is working with crude producers to avoid cancelling or delaying shipments on its damaged Eugene Island pipeline, though a company spokesperson declined to say if force majeure declarations were in the offing.

Texaco reiterated that it expected 100,000 to 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude to be shut in until Thursday at the earliest following a crack on a section of its Eugene Island pipeline in southern Louisiana.
A Texaco spokesman said force majeure conditions were in place, however the company said it was not declaring delays or cancellations at this point.
""We are working with producers to re-direct crudes and get production to shore," said company spokeswoman Maripat Sexton.
Some 47 production platforms feed crude into the Eugene Island system, which runs 176,000 bpd of throughput via the 155-mile long pipeline.
Approximately 50,000 to 70,000 bpd of crude has been diverted away from the final 16-mile section of the pipeline which was affected.
Texaco said it was currently working to retread the damaged section of the pipeline, after crews excavated the forty-foot section where the crack occurred.
"The pipeline will likely return on Thursday. but it may be on Friday," said Texaco's Sexton.
Crews continued to clean-up oil spilled into Lake Barre, where the pipeline lies imbedded in the lake's marshy waters.
"We are into the second phase of clean-up, concentrating our effort on shoreline clean-up. The major skimming operations have been completed, and 2,100 barrels of oil recovered," said Sexton.
The Coast Guard said on Monday that approximately 2,500 barrels of crude leaked into the coastal marsh.
